Persistent high-loss tokens as structural residuals.
Jiang
et al.
(
2026
)
investigate a complementary failure phenomenon: even after OPD training reaches apparent saturation, a substantial subset of tokens (up to 18%) continues to exhibit persistently high loss. These \u201cRock Tokens\u201d resist teacher-driven corrections despite providing a disproportionately large share of total gradient norms due to their high occurrence frequency. Causal intervention shows that Rock Tokens provide negligible functional contribution to actual reasoning performance, suggesting they represent structural and discourse residuals (connectives, formatting, hedging) that the student model cannot or need not internalize from the teacher. The finding implies that a substantial fraction of OPD\u2019s optimization bandwidth is spent on tokens that neither improve nor inform the student\u2019s reasoning capability, complementing TIP\u2019s token-weighting framework (Section
6.1

which
tokens are structurally uninformative rather than merely currently uninformative.
